newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Swedish finance minister sees stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Swedish finance minister sees stability pact deal.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Sunday he expected the June 16-17 EU summit in Amsterdam to reach agreement on the stability pact for economic and monetary union (EMU), but did not rule out negotiations continuing until Tuesday.
"I believe that there are good chances (to reach an agreement)," he told a press briefing.
Asbrink was among European Union finance ministers who were due to meet for an informal dinner to discuss the pact before EU leaders start the summit talks on Monday.

France stunned its partners last week by requesting a delay to study the stability pact, negotiated last December and due to be formally adopted by the Amsterdam summit, and by demanding that a pact for employment and growth of equal weight be added to it.
French and German leaders failed to agree on Friday on a resolution on jobs and growth, leaving the EU finance ministers to seek a solution in Amsterdam.
European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said on Sunday he believed there would be an agreement on the pact on Sunday or Monday.
